ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all proposed shareholders, directors, authorized representatives, and ultimate beneficial owners against the EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, UN Security Council Consolidated List, OFAC SDN and non-SDN sanctions lists, and the Spanish SEPBLAC / Bank of Spain restrictive measures database. Enhanced due diligence is required for any politically exposed person, including source-of-wealth and source-of-funds verification, before the notary may authorize the public deed. Negative screening results are a mandatory precondition to incorporation.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Mercantil Central - Certificacion Negativa de Denominacion Social, available at www.rmc.es; electronic incorporation filing through CIRCE at www.circe.es
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The SL name must be stated in Spanish for registry purposes, although foreign-language company names are permitted if expressed in Latin script and rendered in an unambiguous Spanish transliteration. The name must not be identical or phonetically confusingly similar to any existing Spanish company name, and must clearly evidence corporate form by including 'Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada' or the abbreviation 'SL'.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Within 15 working days from a negative name certificate, the applicant may file written alegaciones with the Registro Mercantil Central for limited reconsideration. If confirmed rejected, the applicant may file an administrative recurso de alzada before the Direccion General de Seguridad Juridica y Fe Publica of the Ministry of Justice within one month of notification. Alternatively, a new application may be submitted with up to three alternative proposed names. The granted name certificate is valid for 90 calendar days and may be renewed once by timely request if incorporation is not completed within the initial window.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office with a physical Spanish street address, mail reception, and management availability is acceptable for initial SL registration for an AI avatar video generation SaaS enterprise. However, if the company claims Spanish tax residence, applies for VAT deductions, or relies on tax treaty benefits, Agencia Tributaria and SEPBLAC may require evidence that management decisions and operational substance occur in Spain. A coworking lease or managed office contract is recommended to establish commercial substance.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low to moderate: approximately 15% probability of an unannounced physical inspection during the first two years for a standard online software SL; the likelihood increases to approximately 35% if substantial VAT refunds, intra-EU triangular transactions, or transfer-pricing positions are claimed. No routine inspection is mandated for unregulated AI software services.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT) — Spanish Tax Agency; digital portal: Sede Electrónica de la AEAT (https://sede.agenciatributaria.gob.es); the AEAT Customs and Excise Directorate operates the export declaration (DUA) window and the EXTEC statistical filing system.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Spanish SL (domestic incorporation): execute the public deed (escritura) before a Spanish notary; file Form 036 (Declaración censal) with AEAT within one month of deed execution to obtain a provisional NIF (for an SL the NIF is a single business letter followed by 8 digits, e.g., B-12345678) and simultaneously enroll in the IVA Census (Censo de empresarios, profesionales y retenedores); register the SL with the Registro Mercantil; then file an updated Form 036 attaching the registry certificate so AEAT can issue the definitive NIF. Foreign non-resident entities taxable in Spain: file Form 036 (or Form 030 where no permanent establishment exists) to obtain a non-resident NIF (NIF-N, format N-XXXXXXXX-X) and, where a permanent establishment is created, append the parent's certificate of tax residence, constitutional documents and appointment of a Spanish tax representative; AEAT issues the provisional NIF in approximately 10 working days and the definitive NIF after verification of the permanent establishment file. A non-established foreign digital service supplier may avoid a Spanish NIF-IVA by electing the OSS mechanism in its Member State of establishment; Spanish VAT nexus nevertheless arises for domestic B2B services, intra-community acquisitions, or B2C electronic services consumed in Spain. Spanish tax residence of the SL follows incorporation, registered office, or place of effective management in Spain (Art. 8 LIS).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: An SL has no US-style check-the-box election and is always a taxable corporate person subject to the Impuesto sobre Sociedades (LIS) on worldwide income; elections available include: (i) the 15% reduced IS rate for newly created SLs engaged in economic activity during the first two tax years (Art. 29.3 LIS); (ii) the reduced-size entity regime of 23% on the first €50,000 of taxable base and 25% above for entities with net turnover below €1,000,000 (Arts. 101–103 LIS); (iii) the optional Consolidated Tax Group regime (Arts. 64–72 LIS) for Spanish parent-subsidiary structures with 75% shareholding and unanimous election; (iv) the VAT group scheme ('Grupo IVA') under Art. 163 septiesdecies LIVA for interdependent entities; and (v) ATAD hybrid mismatch reporting and self-adjustment through Form 55, although the SL itself cannot be classified as fiscally transparent in Spain.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax — Impuesto sobre el Valor Añadido (IVA), governed by Law 37/1992 (LIVA) and Royal Decree 1624/1992
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No general threshold exists for businesses established in Spain: VAT registration and filing are compulsory from the first taxable transaction (Art. 164 LIVA). For non-established sellers there is likewise no statutory threshold; after the abolition of the former €35,000 intra-community distance-selling threshold, the practical registration trigger for non-residents is either direct Spanish VAT registration or participation in the EU OSS Union/non-Union scheme. For the Spanish SL, IVA census registration is effective from the filing of Form 036 regardless of whether turnover has commenced.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Dual real-time digital clearance architecture: (i) SII (Suministro Inmediato de Información del IVA), mandatory for taxpayers with turnover ≥ €6,000,000 and VAT-group members, requires transmission of invoice records to AEAT servers through authenticated XML web-services (SII API) within 4 calendar days of the invoice date (8 calendar days for prompt-payment invoices); (ii) Veri*Factu under Royal Decree 1007/2023 requires all invoice-issuing software to be certified and to generate a QR code and a linked hash-chain (hash encadenado) that irrefutably chains each invoice to the previous one, with automatic transmission of invoice content to AEAT in near real-time — software producers had until 1 July 2025 to adapt; taxpayers with turnover above €8,000,000 must use compliant systems from 1 January 2026, and all other taxpayers from 1 January 2027; B2G invoices must additionally be lodged in Facturae XML format through the FACE platform; Law 18/2022 (Crea y Crece) will extend mandatory e-invoicing to all B2B relationships (large enterprises expected from 2026, SMEs by 2028). Spain does not issue a physical or central digital stamp per invoice; the QR–hash-chain record accepted by AEAT constitutes the algorithmic fiscal seal.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods exported to third countries or tax-free zones are exempt with credit (zero-rated) under Art. 21 LIVA where the exporter holds a valid export declaration (DUA) and transport documents evidencing that the goods left EU customs territory within the periods laid down in the Union Customs Code; services directly linked to exports (Art. 21.2 LIVA) and intra-community B2B supplies to VAT-identified EU customers (Art. 25 LIVA) are likewise fully exempt with credit. For AIGC avatar video SaaS supplied to non-EU B2B customers, the service falls outside the scope of Spanish VAT under the B2B place-of-supply rule of Art. 69 LIVA (customer establishment outside Spain), and is therefore not in-scope rather than zero-rated; B2C supplies of electronic services to EU consumers are taxable in the consumer's Member State under the OSS Union scheme, while B2C supplies to non-EU consumers are outside the scope. The SL must archive customer status, VAT/TIN identification, usage logs, and the foreign-currency settlement trail to substantiate the chosen treatment.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration — DUA (Documento Único Administrativo) accepted and released by Spanish Customs, showing the MRN and the date of exit from EU customs territory
Transport contract, Bill of Lading, CMR airway bill or air waybill evidencing physical dispatch from Spain and arrival outside the EU
Commercial invoice with serialization under Veri*Factu and express legal basis for zero-rating or non-taxability (Art. 21 or Art. 69 LIVA)

Inward Remittance Certificate or foreign-currency bank transfer report evidencing collection of export consideration — no statutory Spanish FX repatriation period is imposed by tax law, but the 180-day commercial benchmark is adopted in this dossier for settlement and transfer-pricing documentation
Packing list and EXTEC statistical filing to Spanish Customs for export dispatches exceeding €1,000 in value, or Intrastat where intra-EU dispatch applies
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: AEAT audits export exemptions by cross-checking SII records, DUA customs data (SIGC/IMPUTA), and bank FX remittance flows; where the documentation set is deficient or fraudulent, the supply is recharacterized as taxable Spanish VAT at 21% with default interest and, if collected via enforcement, a surcharge (recargo de apremio) of 5%–20%; under Arts. 192–193 LGT an inaccurate export zero-rating claim constitutes a serious infringement penalized at 50%–100% of the tax that should have been paid; SII non-compliance carries €200 per missing or incorrect invoice record with a minimum fine of €10,000 per quarterly settlement; under the Anti-Fraud Law 11/2021, issuing invoicing software that is not Veri*Factu-compliant or issuing invoices without the QR/hash seal triggers fines of up to €10,000 per invoice; previously deducted input VAT on export-related acquisitions is retrospectively clawed back with interest; the statute of limitations for assessment is four tax years, extended to ten years where the zero-rating was claimed without the corresponding VAT return being filed or where fraudulent omission is established; criminal tax fraud under Art. 305 of the Criminal Code (defrauded amount exceeding €120,000 per tax period) carries imprisonment of 1–5 years plus fines of 1 to 6 times the defrauded quantity, and aggravated forms under Art. 305 bis (amounts exceeding €600,000 or use of shell structures) carry imprisonment of 2–6 years.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Spain is a Eurozone member and fully liberalized under EU law, the EU Capital Movements Directive, and OECD codes. Both current account and capital account convertibility are unrestricted for residents and non-residents. Profit remittance from an SL to non-resident shareholders is not subject to FX control or prior approval; only standard withholding taxes on dividends and balance-of-payments statistical declarations apply. All EUR and major foreign currency transactions pass freely through the interbank market; there are no exchange surrender requirements, no multiple exchange rates, and no restrictions on external borrowing by a Spanish SL.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No mandatory surrender or conversion rules exist in Spain. A Spanish SL exporting AI video generation SaaS services may retain export proceeds in any currency indefinitely. There is no statutory timeline for repatriation and no conversion ratio. Exporters are only required to report cross-border transactions exceeding EUR 50,000 (or per-account aggregated balances) to the Banco de España for statistical compilation, not for permission or validation.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account and Corporate Treasury Line

Operational Account and Cash Management Platform

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: High for EU/EEA Electronic Money Institutions (EMIs) holding a Spanish branch or passporting under PSD2; they can issue true Spanish IBANs and service a newly formed SL entirely remotely. UK EMIs post-Brexit are medium viability only if they have an EU subsidiary passporting into Spain or require corporate customer to hold a non-Spanish IBAN, creating practical compliance risk. Unlicensed offshore digital EMIs are non-viable and cannot provide the required Spanish statutory bank reference for tax and notarial filings.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is generally mandatory for the director(s) at the first onboarding with branch-based Spanish banks; the same applies for any signing power of attorney granted to third parties. Remote, video-ident KYC is accepted by Spanish online banks (e.g. BNext, EVO Banco) and by Fintech challengers; however, non-resident directors must in most cases complete an in-person biometric verification at a Spanish consulate or a Spanish bank correspondent, and all corporate documents (incorporation deed, NIF certificate, registry certificate) must be apostilled and officially translated into Spanish if executed outside Spain.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High transaction velocity from SaaS subscription platforms (Stripe/Paddle) without traceable end-customer contracts
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide a full transaction ledger mapped to specific license keys, signed enterprise contracts, published price lists, chargeback history, product terms & privacy policy, and a written statement confirming no agents or third-party payment aggregators are involved without KYC.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident shareholders located in more than one jurisdiction or in highly fragmented structure
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Submit a shareholder register, entity chart, register of beneficial owners, tax residency certificates (Modelo 030/036 if applicable), personal KYC documents, source-of-wealth declarations, and a capital injection explanatory note showing the audit trail of all shareholder funds entering Spain.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: AI avatar generation perceived as a high-risk activity for fraud, deepfake misuse, or illicit content monetisation
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Present an AI ethics and abuse prevention policy, editorial/content moderation SOP, IP licensing framework, user-content prohibition clauses, audit-log architecture, and compliance statement under the EU Digital Services Act to demonstrate lawful service operation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Absence of physical office or reliance on virtual office providers
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide a signed registered office lease or virtual-office agreement with the official Company Registry address, proof of director phone/email availability, and detailed operational continuity documentation including software infrastructure and data processing locations.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Shareholder capital injections must be received via SWIFT MT103/MT202 with purpose code 'E001' (Equity capital participation) or 'SI' (Other investment in Spain) under Banco de España's Balance of Payments manual. The SL must retain the notarial deed of capital increase, the share subscription contract, and proof of source of funds. Transactions above EUR 50,000 must be declared to the Banco de España statistical system within the monthly reporting period. For non-EU transfers, a Preal / notificación de operación de inversión may be triggered; the bank will ask for a foreign investment filing via the Registry of Foreign Investments (Registro de Inversiones Exteriores).
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For license fee payments, IP royalty remittances, variable compute costs, and international contractor invoices, use SWIFT MT103 with standard ISO 20022 pain.001 instructions and underlying trade documents (commercial invoice, contract, tax certificate). SEPA Credit Transfer (pacs.008) is mandatory for EUR payments within EEA. For goods-related purchases (e.g. specialised GPU hardware), Documentary Letters of Credit via SWIFT MT700 can be used, but for pure SaaS/AI services the market standard is open-account SWIFT MT103. All outbound transfers above EUR 50,000 require balance-of-payments statistical reporting through the bank or direct SGR declaration.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: EUR/USD and EUR/GBP outright FX forwards (contracts for difference in FX)
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on emerging-market currencies for Latin American receivables (e.g. USD/ARS, USD/MXN, USD/BRL) to cover indirect conversion risk
Cross-currency swaps (EUR/USD, EUR/GBP) for medium-term treasury liabilities and intercompany loans
European-style FX options (EUR call/put pairs) for downside protection on large one-off client invoices
Exchange-traded FX futures on regulated EU venues (Eurex, ICE) for highly liquid USD/EUR and GBP/EUR exposure

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual accounts deposit (Depósito de Cuentas Anuales) in the Mercantile Registry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registro Mercantil (Commercial Registry of the province of the SL's registered office)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Shareholders' approval by 30 June for a 31 December year-end; deposit with the Mercantile Registry within one month after approval, i.e. by 31 July for a calendar-year SL
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Registry late-filing arancel penalties are charged per tariff; after three consecutive years without deposit, the Mercantile Registry closes the company's registry sheet, blocking subsequent registrations until the omission is regularized

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate income tax return (Modelo 200, Impuesto sobre Sociedades)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 25 calendar days after the six-month period following the tax year end; for a calendar-year SL, by 25 July of the succeeding tax year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing surcharge of 5% to 20% of the tax due, depending on delay, plus late-payment interest; inaccurate or incomplete returns may attract additional tax penalties and extend the statutory assessment period

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Related-party transaction annual information return (Modelo 232), where statutory thresholds are met
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Same deadline as Modelo 200; calendar-year filers due by 25 July. Filing is required where transactions with one related party exceed EUR 100,000 in the tax year or total related-party transactions exceed EUR 250,000
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Penalties under the General Taxation Law for late, inaccurate, or omitted data, together with potential transfer-pricing adjustments and tax interest

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual third-party transaction statement (Modelo 347), where statutory thresholds are met
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By 1 March of the year following the calendar year; required where aggregate transactions with any customer or supplier exceed EUR 3,005, or cash transactions with such counterparty exceed EUR 6,000
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Proportionate penalties for omitted or late-filed records, generally starting at EUR 175 per record, with possibility of tax-base verification by the tax authorities

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: An SL must undergo a mandatory independent audit if, for two consecutive financial years, it meets at least two of the following: total assets over EUR 2,850,000; annual net turnover over EUR 5,700,000; average headcount over 50. Mandatory audit also applies to listed, financial, credit, or insurance entities and to groups required to present consolidated accounts; shareholders holding at least 5% of share capital may request an audit
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Individual annual accounts must be prepared under Spanish GAAP as set out in the Plan General de Contabilidad (PGC) approved by Real Decreto 1514/2007 and subsequent updates; consolidated accounts of parent companies are prepared under EU-endorsed IFRS. Annual accounts are presented in euros

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The SL must maintain current beneficial-ownership data and file the annual confirmation in line with the deposit of annual accounts. Any direct or indirect share transfer reaching or exceeding 25% of capital or voting rights must be reported to the Registro de Titularidades Reales / Mercantile Registry system within one month; a nil confirmation is required in years without ownership changes. Failure to keep the UBO register accurate exposes the company to Spanish anti-money-laundering enforcement and penalties
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (Libro Registro de Socios), Register of Directors, Minute Book (Libro de Actas)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 300 - USD 1,200 (registered office, corporate agent, and gestoría/accounting filing support)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 3,500 - USD 12,000 (typical certified audit fee for an SL approaching or above the compulsory audit thresholds)

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Reduced rate of 15% for newly created SL entities in the first two taxable years with positive taxable income (provided the entity engages in an economic activity and meets capitalization requirements); 20% rate for entities with taxable turnover below EUR 1,000,000; 50% reduced tax credit for certain R&D and technological innovation activities applicable to AI software development; patent box regime exempting 50% of qualifying income from certain intangible assets (including AI-related software patents) subject to substance requirements; digital economy tax credits limited to qualifying Spanish-controlled activities.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Modelo 200 (Corporate Income Tax Return) filed via Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT) electronic portal; mandatory electronic filing for all SL entities using XML/SIGI system or certified software (Programa de Ayuda).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 25 calendar days following the six months after the fiscal year-end (i.e., 25th day of the 7th month post year-end; for calendar-year taxpayers: 1–25 July, with the deadline extended to the next business day if the 25th falls on a non-business day).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax identification number of the SL entity (NIF).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter Spanish NIF assigned to the SL; non-resident shareholders do not appear on this box.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Registered corporate name exactly as per Spanish Registry.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the exact registered name; no transliteration adjustments permitted.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Fiscal address in Spain for service of process and tax notices.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Provide an effective Spanish tax address; a virtual office is accepted only if the SL has substance (employees or fixed assets) there.
Use group 933 or 861 for software services; for AI video synthesis SaaS use the appropriate IAE epigraph reflecting ISIC 6201 activities.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Accounting profit or loss before corporate income tax adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Must reconcile with statutory accounts filed at the Mercantile Registry; foreign-source revenue recognized per Spanish GAAP (PGC).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Permanent and temporary differences from accounting base to tax base.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include transfer pricing adjustments, amortization differences, and non-deductible expenses; foreign payments subject to attribution rules.
Include worldwide income for Spanish tax-resident SL; non-resident shareholders are not taxed at entity level.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Full tax liability before credits and withholdings.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply 25% headline rate, reduced 15% for newly created SL where applicable, or 20% small entity rate if turnover below EUR 1,000,000.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 520 / Deducciones para incentivar determinadas actividades
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: R&D tax credits, patent box deductions, and other incentive relief.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only available for qualifying activities carried out in Spain or EEA with supporting technical reports; AI algorithms may qualify if registered with the Spanish Patent and Trademark Office.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net tax liability after credits and double taxation relief.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include foreign tax credits under DTA treaties if the SL has a permanent establishment abroad.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Indicative three installment payments made during the fiscal year.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply the outcome-based method or the base-on-last-year method; must be consistent with Box 300.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Amount due or refundable after offset of installment payments and withholding credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Direct debit to AEAT bank account; refunds require fully verified VAT and transfer pricing submissions.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Anexo C / Balances y estado de cambios en el patrimonio neto
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Balance sheet and statement of changes in equity.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Must include non-resident shareholder loans with market interest; undocumented shareholder advances trigger capitalization rules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Disclosure of related-party transactions exceeding EUR 250,000 per counterparty.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: List all transactions with non-resident affiliates, including SaaS intercompany fees, cloud infrastructure charges, and management fees; attach transfer pricing documentation summary.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing surcharge: 1% per month of the amount payable without surcharge during the first three months; 1.5% per month from the fourth month onward; final surcharge cap 20%. Late filing without amount due: fixed penalty from EUR 200 to EUR 1,500. Failure to file entirely: penalty of 50% of the tax liability (Régimen sancionador, Art. 27 LGT). Formal requisites penalty: EUR 300 to EUR 6,000 per omitted data item. Electronic filing obligation breach: penalty up to EUR 1,500. Interest for late payment: monthly surcharge plus statutory late payment interest (currently 3.75% annual).

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Modelo 100 (for individuals, not applicable to SL); SL entities use Modelo 200 only. Additional regime: Modelo 222 for tax consolidation groups; not applicable to standalone SL.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Not applicable for SL; consolidated groups file within 25 days after 6 months post year-end.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Not applicable for standalone SL; penalties applicable to consolidated groups under Ley del Impuesto sobre Sociedades.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Modelo 202 (Corporate income tax prepayment installment) filed via AEAT electronic portal; required for SL with tax liability exceeding EUR 2,000 in the prior year.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Quarterly (payments in April, October, and December for calendar-year taxpayers)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: 1–20 April, 1–20 October, and 1–20 December for calendar-year fiscal year; for fiscal years ending on other dates, within the first 20 calendar days of the month following the completion of the first, third, and ninth month of the tax period.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 1 / Resultado contable del ejercicio anterior
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Accounting result from the immediately preceding tax year.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use Spanish GAAP audited result, excluding foreign branch results if waived by DTA.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 2 / Cuota íntegra del ejercicio anterior
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Full corporate income tax liability of preceding year.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Exclude withheld foreign taxes not creditable in Spain.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Installments already paid in the current year.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include all three Modelo 202 payments made.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Non-payment or underpayment: surcharge of 20% plus late payment interest; failure to file: fixed penalty EUR 200–1,500 plus surcharge on amounts due.
